records.title: Carry On
records.description: A black and white World War II battlefield image capturing a soldier walking past beach obstacles with a launcher resting across his shoulders. The scene reflects the stark landscape of the Second World War battlefield, where soldiers moved through shattered defenses and open ground in the aftermath of combat. Part of a larger body of WWII battle photography and war zone photography, the composition emphasizes service, endurance, and the quiet burden carried by soldiers across the battlefield. Through restrained light and documentary realism, the image evokes one of the countless battlefield moments that defined scenes from the front during World War II. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Carved Wide
records.description: A fine art painterly landscape photograph of Horseshoe Bend, where the Colorado River carves a broad, deliberate arc through red sandstone at sunset. Rather than spectacle, the image emphasizes scale through restraint — allowing light, negative space, and curvature to guide the eye slowly across the frame. This work treats the landscape as authored geography rather than destination imagery, focusing on atmosphere, proportion, and the quiet authority of form shaped over centuries. Part of a Western American painterly landscape series exploring land as memory rather than monument. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Cotton Candy
records.description: This painterly fine art western landscape photograph captures a fleeting moment of color above the open land near Jackson Hole, Wyoming. A solitary pink cloud drifts across a subdued sky, its softness contrasting with the grounded stillness of the western terrain below. The image is rendered with painterly restraint, emphasizing tone, atmosphere, and quiet balance rather than dramatic scale. Rooted in western landscape photography, the composition treats color as a temporary condition — a brief interruption in an otherwise enduring place. The work invites slow viewing, where subtlety and transience replace spectacle. Part of Wayne Heim’s Western American landscape photography series. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Field Aid
records.description: A black and white World War II battlefield image capturing a medic tending to a wounded soldier in the midst of combat. The scene highlights a quieter side of the Second World War, where battlefield moments were not only defined by fighting, but by the urgent acts of care that unfolded between soldiers under fire. Part of a broader body of WWII battle photography and war zone photography, the composition emphasizes the humanity found within wartime action. Through restrained light and documentary realism, the image reflects the role of medics and the fragile seconds that shaped countless scenes from the front during the Second World War. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Get Ready Boys.
records.description: A painterly World War II photograph capturing a naval officer mid-gesture, signaling movement amid battle-ready machines and waiting men. Controlled light and restrained tonality elevate WWII military equipment and uniformed figures into a cinematic study of authority and anticipation. This work reflects the human force behind mechanical war art, where history’s greatest conflicts turned on gestures as much as firepower. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Hidden by Design
records.description: This painterly fine art landscape photograph from the southern Appalachians explores continuity within the forested landscape, where water, stone, and time operate without interruption. Rendered with softened motion, layered greens, and restrained contrast, the image reflects a painterly landscape photography approach grounded in atmosphere rather than spectacle. Rooted in southern landscape photography, the composition emphasizes persistence over event, allowing the cascading water to function as an ongoing presence rather than a singular focal moment. The scene invites sustained viewing, reinforcing a sense of duration and quiet balance. Part of the Southern Painterly Landscapes series. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Hidden Falls
records.description: Hidden Falls is a painterly fine art landscape photograph of a secluded waterfall tucked deep within a forested hollow in West Virginia. Rather than emphasizing scale or drama, the image is shaped by restraint — where softened water, filtered light, and layered greens create an atmosphere of quiet enclosure. Moss-covered stone and gentle cascades guide the eye inward, encouraging a slower, more intimate reading of the scene. The composition favors immersion over spectacle, allowing the forest itself to feel present, enclosing, and alive. Part of Wayne Heim’s painterly landscape photography series, this work explores stillness, patience, and the quiet moments that exist beyond marked trails and obvious viewpoints. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Left to the Weather
records.description: A painterly fine art landscape photograph set in the Mountain West, this image captures a weathered homestead resting quietly within an open western landscape. Approached with painterly restraint, the work favors atmosphere over spectacle—allowing light, tone, and texture to shape a slow, contemplative narrative. This piece reflects the ethos of painterly Western landscapes and western landscape photography that prioritizes emotional geography over destination. Subtle tonal shifts, softened edges, and layered light invite the viewer to feel every layer of it—where land, structure, and sky share equal weight. Part of a broader Mountain West fine art photography series exploring memory, endurance, and the quiet authority of place. © Wayne Heim

records.title: The Field Keeps One
records.description: This painterly fine art landscape photograph from the Blue Ridge region explores endurance and balance within the southern landscape. Rendered with restrained color, open sky, and a measured composition, the image reflects a painterly landscape photography approach that emphasizes presence over spectacle. Rooted in southern landscape photography, the work treats trees and field as structural elements — vertical and horizontal forces held in equilibrium by time and exposure. The scene invites slow viewing, allowing weather, light, and stillness to share the frame without hierarchy. Part of the Southern Painterly Landscapes series. © Wayne Heim

Rooted in western landscape photography, the composition emphasizes mass, endurance, and quiet interruption. Light does not dominate the scene; it passes through it. records.title: The Weight of Water
records.description: A painterly fine art landscape photograph capturing the quiet force of Black River West Falls in Elyria, Ohio. This work reflects a Midwestern landscape shaped by patience and persistence, where natural forces are felt more than announced. © Wayne Heim

records.description: A rugged cowboy stands on the platform of a moving train car, gripping a rail as he scans the distance with a guarded expression. records.title: WWII Action Art In Fine Art
records.description: A painterly World War II photograph capturing soldiers gathered along the edge of a landing craft as they approach shore. Rather than depicting combat, the image centers on shared resolve and quiet anticipation — the human presence within battle-ready machines. Controlled light and restrained tonality elevate WWII military equipment into a cinematic study of unity, tension, and the moments before action begins. The work reflects the collective experience within history’s greatest conflicts, where courage was often found not alone, but standing beside others facing the same uncertain horizon. © Wayne Heim

records.description: Two men stand together in a wooded landscape, one pointing into the distance while the other follows his line of sight. Both are dressed in period Western clothing, including hats, layered garments, and trail-worn attire. Their posture suggests communication through gesture rather than speech. The natural setting and softened tones create a painterly effect consistent with fine art Western photography. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Young Aide
records.description: A young woman in a Women's Army Corps uniform — a side cap with a light piping on her head, a dark jacket with a collar badge and a shoulder insignia, a white shirt and a tie, her hair in a bun — looks off to the right with a serious expression, a blurred light background of trees behind her at D-Day Conneaut. The black-and-white portrait holds the whole moment in the looking — one woman, one cap, and a gaze that goes past everything. Traditional fine art photography. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Young Girl as Reenactor
records.description: A young girl in Civil War-era dress — a long smock with a wide collar, a knit cap, and a fingerless glove on her hand — leans on a wooden windowsill at Hale Farm with her arms folded, looking off to the side with a pensive expression, the weathered planks of a wooden building behind her. The sepia-black-and-white portrait holds the whole moment in the lean — a girl at a window, and the quiet that comes with it. Traditional fine art photography. © Wayne Heim

records.title: Young Warrior
records.description: A young figure stands near the water's edge, holding a staff upright as his voice breaks into the open air. His posture is lifted and expressive, with movement carried through his raised arm and open mouth. Light softens the scene while revealing detail in the headdress, beadwork, and textures of his clothing, set against the calm surface behind him. © Wayne Heim
